formula.name: Osmanthus Apricot-Suede Chypre — 30mL EdP
formula.body:
# Osmanthus Apricot-Suede Chypre — 30mL EdP

## Character
A warm vintage chypre anchored by osmanthus absolute — apricot-lactonic fruit meets suede leather over classic oakmoss-patchouli bones. The osmanthus bridges the fruity top and leathery base naturally. Think Mitsouko reimagined with an osmanthus heart.

**Family**: Chypre (classic) — bergamot top, oakmoss-patchouli base, floral-fruity heart
**Materials**: 23 (Carles-optimal 15-40 range)
**Concentration**: 16% EdP
**Literature**: Calkin & Jellinek (1994) chypre ratios; Hong et al. (2023) GC-O osmanthus decomposition

## Headspace Physics (Composite OAV Model)

| Voice | OAV | Role |
|-------|--:|------|
| Osmanthus Absolute | **1,326** | Lead character (β-ionone + linalool + dihydro-β-ionone composite) |
| Hedione HC | ~3,900 | Abstract radiance — anosmia-prone, doesn't compete for character recognition |
| Iso E Super | ~2,500 | Skin cocoon — same logic |
| Bergamot FCF | ~1,100 | Chypre framing citrus |

Osmanthus at OAV 1,326 is the loudest IDENTIFIABLE voice — Hedione and Iso E are abstract radiance/cocoon materials that the nose can't name. The osmanthus is clearly "what this smells like."

## Literature-Backed Ratios

| Principle | Source | Target | Applied |
|-----------|--------|--------|---------|
| Bergamot % of concentrate | Calkin & Jellinek (1994) | 20-25% | **8.3%** (reduced — osmanthus leads, not bergamot) |
| Oakmoss active | Carles (1961) | 2-5% | Evernyl compensates under IFRA |
| Fixative loading | Calkin & Jellinek | 15-25% | **16.6%** |
| Musk chord | Ellena (2011) | 3-8% | **5.6%** |

## Formula

| # | Ingredient | Dilution | Amount (µL) | Amount (mL) |
|---|-----------|----------|-------------|-------------|
| **🌅 Top** |
| 1 | Bergamot FCF | neat | 400 | 0.400 |
| 2 | Linalool | neat | 80 | 0.080 |
| **💕 Heart** |
| 3 | Osmanthus Absolute | 10% in DPG | 700 | 0.700 |
| 4 | Rose de Mai Absolute | 10% in DPG | 150 | 0.150 |
| 5 | Jasmine Sambac | 10% in DPG | 60 | 0.060 |
| 6 | Hedione HC | neat | 800 | 0.800 |
| 7 | Apritone | 10% | 80 | 0.080 |
| 8 | Damascone Beta | 10% | 40 | 0.040 |
| 9 | Gamma Decalactone | neat | 40 | 0.040 |
| 10 | Beta Ionone | 1% in TEC | 100 | 0.100 |
| 11 | Parmavert | neat | 20 | 0.020 |
| **🪵 Base** |
| 12 | Iso E Super | neat | 450 | 0.450 |
| 13 | Benzyl Salicylate | neat | 600 | 0.600 |
| 14 | Hexyl Salicylate | neat | 200 | 0.200 |
| 15 | Oakmoss Absolute | 10% in DPG | 250 | 0.250 |
| 16 | Patchouli EO | neat | 150 | 0.150 |
| 17 | Evernyl | 50% in DPG | 30 | 0.030 |
| 18 | Labdanum Resinoid | 10% in DPG | 100 | 0.100 |
| 19 | Suederal | 10% | 200 | 0.200 |
| 20 | Isobutyl Quinoline | 10% | 25 | 0.025 |
| 21 | Ethylene Brassylate | neat | 180 | 0.180 |
| 22 | Romandolide | neat | 150 | 0.150 |
| 23 | Vertofix | neat | 60 | 0.060 |
| 24 | Cedramber | neat | 40 | 0.040 |
| 25 | Guaiacol | 10% | 20 | 0.020 |
| 26 | Timberol | neat | 60 | 0.060 |

**Concentrate total**: 4,985 µL (16.6% of 30mL)
**Materials**: 26 (Carles-optimal 15-40 range)

## Osmanthus GC-O Decomposition (Hong et al., 2023; Guo et al., 2024)

The pipeline decomposes osmanthus absolute into its published constituents:

| Constituent | % in absolute | ODT (ppb) | Role |
|-------------|:---:|:---:|------|
| β-Ionone | 10% | 0.1 | Dominant character — osmanthus identity |
| Dihydro-β-ionone | 8% | 0.3 | Woody-floral backbone |
| Linalool | 8% | 1.5 | Floral-citrus lift |
| Linalool oxide | 6% | 1.0 | Green-floral |
| Phenethyl alcohol | 5% | 200 | Rose body |
| α-Ionone | 3% | 0.5 | Violet-woody |
| γ-Decalactone | 3% | 1.5 | Peach-apricot lactone |
| Geraniol | 3% | 2.0 | Rosy-citrus |
| Hotrienol | 2% | 5.0 | Fresh-floral |
| Theaspirane | 1.5% | 0.1 | Tea-smoke character |
| **Composite OAV** | | | **1,326** |

## Musk Chord (2-axis)

| Axis | Material | Dose | Function |
|------|----------|------|----------|
| Depth | Ethylene Brassylate | 150 neat | Lactonic skin-sit — pairs with osmanthus creaminess |
| Projection | Romandolide | 120 neat | Diffusive outward projection |

## Fixative Gradient

| Layer | Material | Dose | VP |
|-------|----------|------|-----|
| Heavy | Benzyl Salicylate | 600 neat | 0.01 Pa |
| Light | Hexyl Salicylate | 200 neat | 0.03 Pa |

diagnostics: ℹ Very high reservoir fraction — excellent blooming potential
ℹ Dense lipophilic base — deep skin absorption, slow evolution
✓ Strong fabric substantivity — will last well on clothing
Blooming materials (Iso-E-effect): Hexyl Salicylate, Hexyl Salicylate, Patchouli EO, Patchouli EO, Ethylene Brassylate
Hedonic class: pleasant (mean valence +0.66)
✓ >80% of formula mass is hedonically pleasant
Perceptual channels: 20 (10 cross-adaptation groups + 10 solo materials) from 26 ingredients
Channel model: 16 materials collapsed into 10 group channels (Laing ceiling applies to channels, not ingredients)
Active receptor groups (4 with 2+ members):
• salicylate_family: Benzyl Salicylate, Hexyl Salicylate (2 → 1 channel)
• musk: Ethylene Brassylate, Romandolide (2 → 1 channel)
• woody_amber: Iso E Super, Vertofix, Timberol (3 → 1 channel)
• balsamic_smoke: Evernyl, Isobutyl Quinoline, Guaiacol (3 → 1 channel)
Genetic anosmia risk: 3.1% of formula mass affected by OR variants
• Beta Ionone: 8% population (hyposmia, OR5A1)
• Iso E Super: 20% population (hyposmia, OR11H7P)
• Ethylene Brassylate: 6% population (hyposmia, OR2J3)
Distinctiveness index: 0.57
ℹ Subtle cooling chemesthetic undertone
✓ 3 material(s) in optimal character zone
✓ All profiled materials within positive character range
Field distribution: far=20% | mid=66% | near=14%
MW spread: 276 Da (124–400)
Sillage class: moderate
Projection index (mean Kaw): 0.00800
Far-field: Bergamot FCF, Linalool, Parmavert
Mid-field: Osmanthus Absolute, Apritone, Damascone Beta, Gamma Decalactone, Beta Ionone
Near-field: Rose de Mai Absolute, Oakmoss Absolute, Labdanum Resinoid, Ethylene Brassylate, Romandolide
